newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit in range despite some mid-session sell off.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit in range despite some mid-session sell off.

text.p: The ringgit ended rangebound in Kuala Lumpur after two mild dips during the day, dealers said on Thursday.
At mid-session some sell-off from offshore players caused ringgit to go down to 2.5045 per dollar.
Earlier, it fell slightly on selling triggered by an erroneous report which suggested the U.S. would withdraw the Generalised system of preferences privileges from Malaysia.
At 1000 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5023/30 per dollar against 2.5015/18 at close of Kuala Lumpur on Wednesday. It was at 1.7741/58 per Singapore dollar against 1.7751/66.
The ringgit fell 20-30 points after the media report quoted a U.S. trade official as saying that Malaysia would be graduated from the Generalised System of Preferences (GSP) next week.

A U.S. embassy spokesman told Reuters this was not true as Malaysia would move out of the system only on January 1, 1997. "That was the highlight of the day. But, people realised it almost immediately and corrected their positions," a dealer with a Malaysian bank said.
